raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes the `granite4` tool parser dropping streamed text before a tool call when the previous tool call arrived whole in one streamed delta (one line in `Granite4ToolParser._tool_extraction_step`). This carries forward #46934 (@soovittt), which was closed by the stale bot without review.

## Claims

- With `--tool-call-parser granite4`, streamed `content` no longer loses text that comes after a tool call delivered whole in one delta. Before the fix, text arriving in the same delta as the next `<tool_call>` token, ahead of it, was dropped. The tool calls themselves were still emitted, and text in deltas with no `<tool_call>` token still came through.
- This needs a streamed delta that holds a whole `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` (18 tokens for the first call in the render-server test below), for example:
  - `stream_interval` > 1 (`--stream-interval`, or the per-request `stream_interval` field);
  - speculative decoding when one step accepts a whole call (long drafts, e.g. suffix decoding, which defaults to 24 draft tokens);
  - outputs merged when the API server falls behind the engine (`RequestOutputCollector.put`);
  - streaming chat derender chunks (`/v1/chat/completions/derender` with `stream: true`).
- Non-streaming responses and token-by-token streaming were not affected, and their behavior does not change.

## Validation

All runs were on a CPU-only Linux VM (Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, Python 3.12, vLLM built from source for CPU, transformers 5.20.2). For the runs on main, only `vllm/tool_parsers/granite4_tool_parser.py` was replaced with its version on main (5d55ef159); the tests stayed in place.

Online serving, `vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-350m --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser granite4 --enforce-eager --dtype float32 --max-model-len 2048`. The request asks for the weather in Paris and Rome with one `get_weather` tool. To give main and this branch the same tokens, the output is pinned with `structured_outputs: {"choice": [...]}` to `Sure.<tool_call>{... "Paris" ...}</tool_call> Now Rome.<tool_call>{... "Rome" ...}</tool_call>`. The only difference between the streaming requests is `stream_interval`:

| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | main: `content` | this branch: `content` |
|---|---|---|
| non-streaming | `'Sure. Now Rome.'` | `'Sure. Now Rome.'` |
| `stream: true` (13 chunks) | `'Sure. Now Rome.'` | `'Sure. Now Rome.'` |
| `stream: true`, `stream_interval: 64` (3 chunks) | `'Sure.'` | `'Sure. Now Rome.'` |

Every response has both tool calls (`{"city": "Paris"}`, `{"city": "Rome"}`) and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. With `stream_interval: 64`, the last chunk on main is `('.', 2 tool-call deltas)`; on this branch it is `('. Now Rome.', 2 tool-call deltas)`.

New tests, both without mocks:
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py::test_tool_call_parser_complex[1000-1000]`: a new chunk size for the existing streaming test. 1000-character chunks put every tool call of its input in one delta, and the test asserts the exact streamed content and tool calls.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_granite4_content_after_whole_tool_call_chunk` runs through the GPU-less render server, so it is deterministic and needs no GPU or weights:
  1. `RemoteLaunchRenderServer` runs `vllm launch render ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser granite4`.
  2. `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` with one `get_weather` tool returns the prompt `token_ids`.
  3. The test encodes `<tool_call>{... "Paris" ...}</tool_call> Now Rome.<tool_call>{... "Rome" ...}</tool_call>` with the model's tokenizer. `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>` are single tokens (100270, 100271).
  4. Two streaming `POST /v1/chat/completions/derender` calls follow: chunk 1 is the 18 tokens of the first call, and chunk 2 is the other 22 tokens. Each chunk is one `Parser.parse_delta` call through `ChatStreamProcessor`, the processor `/v1/chat/completions` streaming uses. The test asserts content `" Now Rome."` and both tool calls.

Unit test file on main:

```
$ python -m pytest -v -p no:cacheprovider tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py
tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py::test_tool_call_parser_complex[1000-1000] FAILED [100%]
E       AssertionError: assert 'Here goes th...ul assistant.' == 'Here goes th...ul assistant.'
E         
E           Here goes the bbox call: 
E         -  Now the stock price call: 
E         -   Now another bbox call: 
E         ? -
E         +  Now another bbox call: 
E             See? I'm a helpful assistant.
FAILED tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py::test_tool_call_parser_complex[1000-1000]
=================== 1 failed, 4 passed, 2 warnings in 2.99s ====================
```

On this branch:

```
$ python -m pytest -v -p no:cacheprovider tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py
tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py::test_tool_call_parser_complex[1000-1000] PASSED [100%]
======================== 5 passed, 2 warnings in 4.51s =========================
```

Render-server test on main (excerpt):

```
$ python -m pytest -v -s -p no:cacheprovider tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_granite4_content_after_whole_tool_call_chunk
INFO:     127.0.0.1:49426 - "POST /v1/chat/completions/render HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:49426 - "POST /v1/chat/completions/derender HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:49426 - "POST /v1/chat/completions/derender HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
E       AssertionError: assert None == ' Now Rome.'
FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_granite4_content_after_whole_tool_call_chunk
======================== 1 failed, 2 warnings in 22.83s ========================
```

On this branch:

```
$ python -m pytest -v -s -p no:cacheprovider tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_granite4_content_after_whole_tool_call_chunk
======================== 1 passed, 2 warnings in 31.96s ========================
```

The whole derender stream file. The only failure on main is the new test. The xfail on both sides is the existing `test_stream_parsed_matches_batch_reasoning[triples]` (vllm#55195).

```
$ python -m pytest -v -s -p no:cacheprovider tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
# main
FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_granite4_content_after_whole_tool_call_chunk
======= 1 failed, 121 passed, 1 xfailed, 2 warnings in 118.06s (0:01:58) =======
# this branch
============ 122 passed, 1 xfailed, 2 warnings in 173.92s (0:02:53) ============
```

The 7 `Granite4ToolParser` cases in `tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py` give the same result on main and on this branch (6 passed, 1 existing skip).

`pre-commit run --files vllm/tool_parsers/granite4_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py` passes (ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy, check-test-tethering).

CI coverage:
- The unit test runs in the `cpu-tool-parsers` step (`pytest -v -s tool_parsers`). Its source_file_dependencies include `vllm/tool_parsers/` and `tests/tool_parsers`.
- The render-server test runs in the `entrypoints-integration-api-server` step (`pytest -v -s entrypoints/scale_out`, sharded). Its source_file_dependencies include `vllm/` and `tests/entrypoints/scale_out`. The existing `RemoteOpenAIServer` granite4 test (`tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py`) needs real weights and streams with the default `stream_interval` of 1.

## Details

- Root cause (`vllm/tool_parsers/granite4_tool_parser.py`, `_tool_extraction_step`, line 185):
  - The "entering a new tool call" branch sets `self.in_tc = True`. When the `</tool_call>` token is in the same buffer, it emits the call but then reset `self.start_in_tc`, an attribute that is written only there and read nowhere, instead of `self.in_tc`.
  - The parser therefore stayed in tool-call mode after the call. The next buffer with a `<tool_call>` token went to the "between start and end" or "found the end" branch. Neither emits the text before the start token, so that text was dropped.
- Fix: reset `self.in_tc = False`. The sibling end-of-call branch a few lines below already does this after cutting out a call.
- Why the existing tests missed it: `test_tool_call_parser_complex` used 1-20 character chunks, so a whole `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` never landed in one delta.
- No model eval. The change does not alter generated tokens, tool calls or non-streaming responses. It only restores streamed text the parser dropped.
- No docs change. This restores the documented behavior of `--tool-call-parser granite4` (`docs/features/tool_calling.md`) and adds no flag, field or default.
- Not included:
  - The Rust frontend parser `rust/src/parser/src/tool/json/granite4.rs`, a separate implementation without this flag.
  - Malformed output with a stray `</tool_call>` before a `<tool_call>` in the same delta. `_tool_extraction_step` searches for the end token from the start of the buffer (line 162), so main already mis-streams such a delta (it can drop text); non-streaming rejects this output and returns it as plain content. With this fix, the text between the stray end token and the start token is streamed twice. Searching for the end token after the start token would address that; I kept it out of this fix.
  - Other tool parsers.
- This carries forward #46934 by @soovittt, which was stale-closed with no review. The fix is the same line. The tests differ: a chunk size added to the existing streaming test instead of a new unit test, plus the render-server test.
- Not a duplicate:
  - `gh pr list --state all --search` for `start_in_tc` and for `_tool_extraction_step` finds only #46934.
  - Searches for `Granite4ToolParser` (all states) and `granite4` (open PRs) find no other PR that changes this branch. #47955 (gigachat3, granite, granite-20b-fc), #48295 (llama3_json, jamba, ernie45) and #48348 (internlm2) handle whole tool calls in one delta for other parsers.
  - Of all open PRs, only #54964 touches `vllm/tool_parsers/granite4_tool_parser.py`. It changes `dump_args` only, and its head still has the `start_in_tc` line.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

@@ -2780,3 +2780,58 @@ async def test_stream_parsed_missing_prompt_token_ids_rejected(parser_client):
     )
     assert resp.status_code == 400
     assert "prompt_token_ids" in resp.json()["error"]["message"]
+
+
+GRANITE4_MODEL = "ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def granite4_server():
+    args = ["--enable-auto-tool-choice", "--tool-call-parser", "granite4"]
+    with RemoteLaunchRenderServer(GRANITE4_MODEL, args) as remote_server:
+        yield remote_server
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_stream_parsed_granite4_content_after_whole_tool_call_chunk(
+    granite4_server,
+):
+    """Text before a tool call is streamed when the previous tool call
+    arrived whole in one chunk (a multi-token engine step)."""
+    tokenizer = get_tokenizer(GRANITE4_MODEL)
+    first_ids = tokenizer.encode(
+        '<tool_call>{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}'
+        "</tool_call>",
+        add_special_tokens=False,
+    )
+    rest_ids = tokenizer.encode(
+        ' Now Rome.<tool_call>{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Rome"}}'
+        "</tool_call>",
+        add_special_tokens=False,
+    )
+    chat_request = {
+        "model": GRANITE4_MODEL,
+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Paris, then Rome?"}],
+        "tools": _PARSER_TOOLS,
+        "tool_choice": "auto",
+    }
+
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
+        base_url=granite4_server.url_for(""), timeout=60.0
+    ) as client:
+        resp = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions/render", json=chat_request)
+        assert resp.status_code == 200, resp.text
+        prompt_token_ids = resp.json()["token_ids"]
+        streamed = await stream_chat_derender(
+            client,
+            first_ids + rest_ids,
+            [len(first_ids), len(rest_ids)],
+            chat_request,
+            len(prompt_token_ids),
+            prompt_token_ids,
+        )
+
+    assert streamed["content"] == " Now Rome."
+    assert [
+        (tc["name"], json.loads(tc["arguments"])) for tc in streamed["tool_calls"]
+    ] == [("get_weather", {"city": "Paris"}), ("get_weather", {"city": "Rome"})]
